task.description:
WF-03 Step 3b: HARD GATE on DOC-UPDATER's amendment for ISS-0117, landed as commit 131aba9 (docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2/§3/new §4.1, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md §5/new §7.2). Read the diff — `git show 131aba9` — and the two files as they now stand.

You are gating a change to the pipeline's OWN RULES, which is the class where this gate has earned its keep: on ADHOC-20260821-002, REVIEWER FAILED the first pass on a BLOCKER ORCH itself had authored, corrected ORCH's framing of its own question, and caught a hazard inside the very rule meant to prevent that hazard. A PASS here is not the expected outcome; a re-derived verdict is.

RE-DERIVE, DO NOT INHERIT. The amendment cites specific measurements as its justification, and `docs/anti-patterns.md`'s 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' has now fired four times in this project — twice on records that were plausible, confidently worded and wrong. The producing handoff's claims and the Step 1 diagnosis are both records. Check at minimum these six, each with a command:
  (i) `handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json`'s `orch_restart_note` really does rule that `rework_count` was NOT incremented, and really does give the reason §4.1(a-1) attributes to it. If the amendment put words in that file's mouth, that is a finding.
  (ii) The 'three key names, five occurrences, two key positions, two shapes' claim in §3 and §4.1(b). Count them yourself across `handoffs/`.
  (iii) `handoffs/WF02-REQ043-20260818/step-final-git-merge.json` is genuinely `PENDING` with a null `result`, and PR #174 / `e25822a` genuinely landed on main. The whole rejection of the 'leave it IN_PROGRESS' option rests on this one file.
  (iv) `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json`'s `completed_at` is genuinely byte-identical to its `orch_reconstruction.reconstructed_at`, and `orch_reconstruction` genuinely does NOT declare `completed_at` among the fields it wrote.
  (v) ISS-0033's resolution genuinely established the `-resume` append precedent §7.2 attributes to it, including that the original entry staying BLOCKED was ruled deliberate. §7.2 reconciles a new rule against that precedent; if the precedent says something else, the reconciliation is wrong.
  (vi) The '15 files violate §2's status enum' claim used in §4.1(b) to argue that writing a rule down is necessary-but-not-sufficient.

THEN GATE ON THESE, which are the failure modes specific to this change:

(1) ALL FOUR QUESTIONS, ACTUALLY DECIDED. ISS-0117 poses four and says explicitly not to assume its own candidate convention is right. Check each is DECIDED, not merely discussed, and that the amendment does not silently adopt ISS-0117's candidate where the Step 1 diagnosis measured something different. Q1 who may complete it; Q2 the mandatory marking; Q3 mid-action vs after-acting; Q4 the registry record.

(2) READ §2, §3 AND §4.1 AGAINST EACH OTHER, NOT EACH ALONE. This is a named, recent failure of this exact gate — see `docs/anti-patterns.md`'s 'Validating a design's type table for well-formedness instead of against its own normative section', where CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR passed a design TWICE because each section was internally well-formed and nothing was checked ACROSS them in the direction the design itself declared authoritative. Here §4.1 declares itself the exception to §3 and §4, and §2's JSON block restates the field's shape. So: list every member §4.1(b)'s table requires, and check each against §2's block; check §3's new rows and their exception pointers against what §4.1 actually says; check §4.1's own cross-reference to ORCHESTRATOR §7.2 resolves to what is there. Any restatement is a place the document can contradict itself, and the schema block is the likeliest to drift because it is written once and never re-read.

(3) INSTRUCTION PRECEDENCE — RE-RUN IT YOURSELF. DOC-UPDATER reports a nil result from four greps and one adjacent hit (`WF-01_requirement_development.md:102`) which it closed inside ORCHESTRATOR.md §5. Do not accept that; re-run it. `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` is RANK 4 in core-directives.md's chain — below role files (rank 2) and workflow docs (rank 3) — so a mandatory rule placed there is out-ranked by any permissive text above it. This is precisely the BLOCKER shape ADHOC-20260821-002's first gate caught. Search `.claude/agents/*.md`, `docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md`, `docs/agents/protocols/*.md` and `core-directives.md` for anything that permits what §4.1 forbids, or that instructs an agent to do what §4.1 now reserves to ORCH.

(4) THE §5 REWORK-COUNTER EDIT IS A LOOPHOLE RISK — scrutinise it specifically. Scoping `rework_count` to 'rejected work' is correct for the death case, but check it cannot be read as licence to skip incrementing in ordinary cases. A rule that narrows a counter is exactly the shape that quietly disables an escalation budget, and `max_rework` is what stops an agent looping forever.

(5) NO GATE WEAKENED, NO DETECTOR EDITED. §4.1 and §7.2 both touch bookkeeping rules that exist to catch corruption. Confirm append-only (`HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` §5, core-directives 'Bookkeeping Is Not Optional'), §7.1's re-read-before-write, and 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' are all intact and not narrowed by the additions. §7.2 says adding a field to an entry is not rewriting history — rule on whether that is a fair reading or an erosion.

(6) THE OPTIONAL-BY-ABSENCE DESIGN. §4.1(b) makes the field's ABSENCE carry the assertion 'this result is the acting agent's own report', and forbids backfill. Rule on whether that is sound given 534 pre-existing files that predate the rule and were never audited — absence there means 'the rule did not exist yet', not 'attested'. If that is a real ambiguity, say what would close it. Do not manufacture a finding if it is genuinely fine.

(7) SCOPE. Only the two owned files may be changed. Confirm the ISS-0192 stale handoffs were NOT retroactively repaired, `docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml` was NOT edited, and no registry/log file was touched by DOC-UPDATER. Also rule on DOC-UPDATER's own self-reported MINOR: it added `//` comments to §2's JSON block, making it non-parseable — it notes the block already contained placeholders and was never parseable. Is that acceptable in a schema block agents read as a contract?

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL, with every failed check named by number and the specific gap stated, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's `validator-fail` worked example. A FAIL routes back to DOC-UPDATER as rework iteration 1 of 3. You may NOT edit the two doc files yourself — you are the gate, not the producer. Write only this handoff file. Do not call `gh` or the queue; report findings needing an id in `result.issues` and ORCH allocates.
acceptance_criteria: All six re-derivation checks (i)-(vi) were run with actual commands, and the commands and their outputs are quoted in result.summary — not summarised as 'verified'
Checks (1)-(7) each carry an explicit verdict; an unlisted check reads as an unrun check

Check (2) is answered by listing §4.1(b)'s required members and diffing them against §2's JSON block member by member, and by resolving §3's exception pointers and §4.1's cross-reference to ORCHESTRATOR §7.2 — not by reading each section in isolation
Check (3)'s greps were re-run independently of DOC-UPDATER's; the patterns used are quoted, and a nil result is stated as a measured finding

Any divergence between the amendment's cited evidence and what the source files actually say is reported at BLOCKER or MAJOR — a rule justified by a misquoted incident is worse than no rule, because the next agent inherits the misquote
The verdict is re-derived from the two doc files and the sources they cite, never from DOC-UPDATER's result.summary
No file outside handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json is modified by this step; `git status --porcelain` is quoted

result.summary:
VERDICT: FAIL. Re-derived from commit 131aba9, from docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md as they now stand, and from the source files they cite -- never from DOC-UPDATER's result.summary. 4 of the 7 gate checks pass; checks (2), (6) and (7) fail, and re-derivation check (ii) fails. 1 BLOCKER, 4 MAJOR, 3 MINOR below.

=== SIX RE-DERIVATION CHECKS, EACH WITH ITS COMMAND ===

(i) PASS. `python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json'))"` -> top-level keys are the 17 schema keys plus `orch_restart_note` at position 18/18, type `str`. Its text reads verbatim: "rework_count deliberately NOT incremented: ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5's rework counter tracks rejected work, and nothing was rejected here; treating an infra termination as rework would burn a max_rework budget that exists to catch a producer repeating a mistake." and "The handoff was left IN_PROGRESS with a null result and was never committed, so no partial verdict entered the audit trail." Both the ruling AND the reason 4.1(a-1) attributes to it are genuinely there, and the quoted fragments in 4.1(a-1)'s blockquote and in ORCHESTRATOR section 5's new paragraph are accurate. No words put in that file's mouth.

(ii) FAIL -- see BLOCKER-1. `grep -rlE '"orch_(restart_note|timestamp_correction|reconstruction)"' handoffs/` -> exactly 4 files. A full non-schema-top-level-key scan over all 547 handoff JSON files (`json.load` on every `handoffs/**/*.json`, subtracting the 17 keys section 2 defines; 0 unparseable) confirms: orch_timestamp_correction 2, orch_restart_note 1, orch_reconstruction 1 = FOUR occurrences, in FOUR files, in FOUR runs. Sorted by each file's completed_at:
  2026-08-16T18:49:40Z WF02-REQ023 orch_timestamp_correction str pos 18/18
  2026-08-16T21:35:39Z WF02-REQ027 orch_restart_note          str pos 18/18
  2026-08-17T19:45:30Z WF02-REQ037 orch_timestamp_correction  str pos 11/18
  2026-08-21T03:29:36Z WF03-ISS0109 orch_reconstruction      dict pos 18/18
So: THREE key names -- CONFIRMED. TWO key positions (18 and 11) -- CONFIRMED. TWO shapes (bare string x3, object x1) -- CONFIRMED. "FIVE occurrences" -- REFUTED, it is four; "across FOUR runs" -- REFUTED in both readings (four key-bearing runs, or five death incidents across FIVE runs per the Step 1 diagnosis's own enumeration REQ027/REQ023/REQ037/REQ043/ISS0109). "changed shape from a bare string to a structured object between its FIRST AND SECOND use" -- REFUTED: the object appears on the FOURTH use, three uses and five days after the first. Details and impact in BLOCKER-1.

(iii) PASS. `python -c "...json.load('handoffs/WF02-REQ043-20260818/step-final-git-merge.json')"` -> status='PENDING', completed_at=None, result=null (the whole block, not merely result.status), and no non-schema top-level key. `git log --oneline -1 e25822a` -> "e25822a feat(WF02-REQ043): instance-engine schema -- instance_projections ALTER, tokens, tasks (#174)"; `git merge-base --is-ancestor e25822a main` -> true. The PR number in the commit subject is #174 as cited. The rejection of the "leave it IN_PROGRESS" option rests on a claim that is true as stated.

(iv) PASS. `python` over handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json -> completed_at == '2026-08-21T03:29:36Z' and orch_reconstruction.reconstructed_at == '2026-08-21T03:29:36Z', equality test True (byte-identical). orch_reconstruction's members are exactly ['reconstructed_by','reconstructed_at','reason','commands_run','not_verifiable_after_the_fact'] -- there is NO member enumerating written fields (filter for any key containing 'field'/'written'/'wrote' -> []), so it genuinely does not declare completed_at among what it wrote. Section 3's new paragraph and 4.1(b)'s closing sentence are accurate. Also re-checked the derived claim in 4.1(b): that file's status is COMPLETED, result.status is PASS, artifacts_out has 1 entry -- so "nothing in status, completed_at, result.status or result.artifacts_out distinguishes that file from a normal completion" is true as written.

(v) PASS. `cat docs/issues/ISS-0033.yaml` -> resolution reads: "found a second entry, run_id \"WF03-ISS0030-20260817-resume\", status: COMPLETED, released_lock: true, appended by commit 0a34f79 exactly as that commit's own message states (\"records the resume run in orchestrator.log/registry.json -- original BLOCKED entry left untouched, append-only\"). The original WF03-ISS0030-20260817 entry staying BLOCKED forever is deliberate, correct append-only history (the run really was blocked at that point in time, on that specific attempt) -- not a bookkeeping gap." Every element ORCHESTRATOR section 7.2 attributes to ISS-0033 is present: the -resume run_id suffix, the SEPARATE APPENDED entry, commit 0a34f79, status COMPLETED, and the explicit ruling that the original staying BLOCKED was deliberate. The quoted clause in 7.2 is verbatim. The reconciliation is built on a precedent that says what 7.2 says it says.

(vi) PASS, with a precision note (MINOR-3). Scan over all 547 handoff files against section 2 line 89's enum (PENDING|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|FAILED|ESCALATED|CANCELLED) -> 13 files carry an illegal top-level status, all of them "PASS" (11 files of WF02-REQ063-20260818 plus WF02-REQ064-20260818 step-01 and step-02a), and 2 further files (WF02-REQ059/WF02-REQ060 step-00-git-setup.json) have NO top-level `status` key at all and sit on a foreign flat schema. 13 + 2 = the cited 15, and the parenthetical honestly claims only 13 for "PASS", so 4.1(b)'s necessary-but-not-sufficient argument stands on real data. The same scan independently returns 13 files carrying a non-schema top-level key -- distinct from the 15, and not conflated in the amendment's text.

=== SEVEN GATE CHECKS ===

(1) ALL FOUR QUESTIONS ACTUALLY DECIDED -- PASS. Read docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml's "WHAT A FIX SHOULD DECIDE" list against section 4.1 and ORCHESTRATOR 7.2. Q1 (who may complete it): DECIDED as a split keyed to a probe -- (a-1) fresh instance of the same role, (a-2) ORCH only -- and it does NOT silently adopt ISS-0117's candidate: the issue's own conduct was ORCH-writes-the-block, and the amendment reaches ORCH-only for one branch and a fresh same-role instance for the other, refuting "nobody" by measurement rather than preference. Q2 (mandatory marking): DECIDED as a required top-level field with a fixed name and fixed six-member shape, not a convention. Q3 (mid-action vs after-acting): DECIDED as materially different paths selected by a mandatory probe of declared side effects, with indeterminate falling to (a-1). Q4 (should last_known_step record agent death): DECIDED, and decided AGAINST the issue's framing -- discrete `recovered`/`recovery_note` fields instead, with last_known_step defined and explicitly scoped to exclude interruption/recovery narrative. Four of four decided, none left to a general statement.

(2) SECTIONS 2, 3 AND 4.1 READ AGAINST EACH OTHER -- FAIL. See MAJOR-2, MAJOR-3, MINOR-1.
  Member-by-member diff of 4.1(b)'s table against section 2's JSON block (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md lines 128-135 vs lines 377-384): reconstructed_by / reconstructed_at / reason / fields_written / evidence / not_verifiable_after_the_fact. Six required by 4.1(b), six present in section 2, names identical, order identical, no member in one and absent from the other. THAT part is clean -- the schema block did not drift on membership.
  It drifted on MODALITY (MINOR-1): section 2's comment says the field is "present ONLY on a handoff recovered under section 4.1", which covers both branches, while 4.1(a-1) says explicitly that a redispatch writes NO marker. Section 2 also labels the field "OPTIONAL" where 4.1(b) says "MUST".
  Section 3's exception pointers do NOT all resolve (MAJOR-2): the table sends `completed_at`, `status` and `result` to section 4.1, but 4.1(a-2) grants ORCH only the `result` block in normative text -- ORCH's authority over `completed_at` and over the COMPLETED `status` exists only as an illustrative example inside 4.1(b)'s `fields_written` row. The one field whose undeclared reconstruction is the amendment's own motivating incident is the one its new exception clause never explicitly licenses.
  Section 4.1's cross-reference to ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.2 (4.1(d)) DOES resolve: 7.2 exists, defines `recovered` and `recovery_note`, and states which of the two registry mechanisms applies when, in both directions. That pointer is sound.
  4.1's parenthetical about ISS-0192 does not survive being read against its cited source (MAJOR-3).

(3) INSTRUCTION PRECEDENCE, RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY -- PASS, nil result, stated as a measured finding. Re-read core-directives.md lines 127-140 first: rank 1 handoff task, 2 .claude/agents/<role>.md, 3 docs/agents/workflows/WF-0N_*.md, 4 protocol docs INCLUDING docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, 5 core-directives.md, 6 CLAUDE.md. I widened DOC-UPDATER's file set to include docs/agents/protocols/*.md, which its greps 1-3 omitted. Set actually searched (26 files, listed by `ls`): .claude/agents/*.md (16), docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md (5), docs/agents/protocols/*.md (4), docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md.
  Pattern A -- `grep -rniE "on behalf|fill in (the )?result|writes? the result (block|for)|complete the handoff for|reconstruct|not_agent_attested|attested"` -> ZERO lines (exit 1). Nothing at rank 1-3, and nothing in the rank-4 protocol docs, permits any agent to author another agent's result.
  Pattern B -- `grep -rniE "\b(died|dies|death|crashed|crash|terminated|terminates)\b|api error|session limit|power outage|interrupted|orphan|stale handoff"` -> 8 lines, ALL non-conflicting on inspection: 5 are "orphaned depends_on" / "orphaned erl.exe processes", 1 is security-reviewer.md's "terminates validation with status FAIL", and 2 are TASK_QUEUE.md:305/344 about re-claiming or force-releasing a QUEUE TASK after a host crash -- queue-lock mechanics, which say nothing about who writes a handoff result. So the agent-death concept is genuinely absent from ranks 1-3, which is what makes 4.1's rank-4 placement survivable: there is no higher-ranked text covering the same case more permissively.
  Pattern C -- `grep -rn "rework_count"` -> 2 lines. WF-01_requirement_development.md:102 (rank 3) reads "Same as `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 5: on FAIL, ORCH increments `rework_count`" -- it is both conditioned on FAIL and explicitly deferential to section 5, so it cannot out-rank the new scoping; DOC-UPDATER's assessment reproduces. GIT_MERGE.md:293 (rank 4, NOT found by DOC-UPDATER) reads "`rework_count` applies; `max_rework = 3` before ESCALATED" -- read in context it is scoped to "When this step FAILs due to a complex conflict", i.e. conditioned on a FAIL verdict, so again no conflict. Nil confirmed by measurement, not by silence.
  Pattern D -- `grep -rniE "last_known_step|recovery_note|\brecover"` over the same set plus docs/agents/shared/*.md -> the only definitional hits are the new ones in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md; TASK_QUEUE.md's four hits are queue-recovery mechanics. Nothing competes with 7.2's definition.
  OBSERVATION, not a finding against this change (MINOR-2): docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md -- which now carries two of the five changes, including the rework-counter scoping -- does not appear ANYWHERE in core-directives.md's six-rank chain. That is pre-existing and out of this run's scope, but it means the rank of section 5's new paragraph and of section 7.2 is undefined, and DOC-UPDATER's "closed the ambiguity at the source" fix lands in an unranked document.

(4) THE SECTION 5 REWORK-COUNTER EDIT -- PASS. Re-read ORCHESTRATOR.md lines 116-149 in full. The addition narrows in exactly one direction and cannot be read as general licence: it restates that "Every rule above is conditioned on a FAIL verdict", and the single exemption it grants is named by rule reference -- "not incremented when a handoff is re-stamped and redispatched under HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4.1(a-1)" -- not by a judgement predicate like "when the agent had trouble". The exemption is unreachable by a producer trying to dodge the budget: 4.1(a-1) is triggered by ORCH observing a death and re-stamping, the acting agent by definition wrote nothing, and any step that DID reach a FAIL verdict before dying is still inside "On FAIL". No escalation budget is disabled. The paragraph also states its own trigger condition ("an agent reading step 3 above in isolation could reasonably read a 4.1 redispatch as falling under it"), so a future reader can tell when it applies.

(5) NO GATE WEAKENED, NO DETECTOR EDITED -- PASS. `git show 131aba9 --stat` and the full diff: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 5 (append-only), section 6 (never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures), and ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.1 (re-read-before-write, no force push) are untouched -- 4.1 was inserted between section 4 and section 5, and 7.2 after 7.1, with no deletions in either file except the three-row timestamp table replaced by the five-row one. RULING ON "adding a field to an entry is not rewriting history": that is a FAIR reading, not an erosion, and I checked it three ways. (a) Against HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 5's actual test -- "they must never shrink... a commit that reduces either file's size is a defect" -- adding a field grows the entry. (b) Against 7.1's actual prohibition -- "Never overwrite, reorder, or re-serialise ANOTHER SESSION's entry" -- 7.2's amend branch is scoped to same-session recovery of the run's OWN entry, so it never reaches another session's; the later-session branch appends rather than amends, which is precisely 7.1-safe and is ISS-0033's precedent. (c) 7.2 re-imposes rather than relaxes: it repeats 7.1's re-read-immediately-before-writing requirement by name and adds "If the entry to be amended is not the last one, or another session has written since your read, re-read and re-derive before touching it." Net effect on the detectors is neutral-to-tightening.

(6) THE OPTIONAL-BY-ABSENCE DESIGN -- FAIL. See MAJOR-4. The ambiguity is real and it is already instantiated on disk, not hypothetical: `grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/` today returns only this run's own step-01 and step-03 handoffs (which merely discuss the field) and NOT WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json, which is the one genuine reconstruction in the repository. So the enumeration command 4.1(b) offers as the field's whole justification returns zero reconstructions in a repository containing one, and 4.1(b)'s no-backfill rule freezes that.

(7) SCOPE -- FAIL on the JSON-block ruling; PASS on confinement. `git show --name-only --format= 131aba9` -> exactly docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md, docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03-amendment.json. No registry, no log, no issue file. `git log --oneline -2 -- docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml` -> last touched by 5aa775d, NOT by 131aba9, so ISS-0117.yaml was not edited. ISS-0192's two stale handoffs were NOT retroactively repaired: WF02-REQ043 step-final still reads status PENDING / completed_at null / result null, and WF02-REQ062 step-03 still reads status PENDING. RULING ON THE `//` COMMENTS: NOT acceptable, and the stated justification is measurably false -- BLOCKER... see MAJOR-1. `git status --porcelain` at the end of this step, quoted verbatim:
 M handoffs/orchestrator.log
 M handoffs/registry.json
?? docs/issues/ISS-0190.yaml
?? docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml
?? docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml
?? handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json
The first five are ORCH's own dispatch-time writes, expected per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 7 and left untouched by this step. The sixth is this gate's own handoff, the only file I wrote. The two doc files under review show no modification -- I did not edit them.

=== WHAT PASSES, SO REWORK DOES NOT UNDO IT ===
The diagnosis of the root cause is right and the shape of the fix is right: section 3's table WAS the defect, the four questions ARE all decided, the probe-based mid-vs-after discrimination with indeterminate falling to redispatch is sound and total, the rework-counter scoping is correct and loophole-free, the ISS-0033 reconciliation is accurate in both directions, and nothing weakens append-only or 7.1. Every finding below is a correction to evidence or to cross-section wording. None of them requires re-deciding anything.

issues.description: CHECK (ii)/(2). The measurement that justifies the required-field-over-convention decision is misstated, in two places, and is self-contradicted by its own parenthetical. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md line 260 says "five occurrences across four runs, under three different ad-hoc top-level key names (orch_restart_note, orch_timestamp_correction x2, orch_reconstruction)" -- the parenthetical enumerates FOUR. Line 394 repeats it as "three key names across five occurrences (orch_timestamp_correction twice, orch_restart_note, orch_reconstruction)" -- again four. MEASURED (json.load over all 547 handoff files, subtracting section 2's 17 keys): there are FOUR occurrences of an ad-hoc recovery/correction key, in FOUR files, in FOUR runs. The fifth incident in the Step 1 diagnosis's count is WF02-REQ043-20260818, which carries NO such key -- it is the unrepaired case 4.1(a-2) cites as the counter-example, so it is not an instance of the convention at all. The diagnosis's own phrase "five occurrences across four runs" is internally wrong too (it enumerates five run ids), and it was inherited rather than re-derived. SECOND ERROR, same paragraph: "changed shape from a bare string to a structured object between its FIRST AND SECOND use", closed by "A convention that changed shape on its second application is not a convention." Sorted by completed_at the four uses are REQ023 2026-08-16T18:49:40Z str, REQ027 2026-08-16T21:35:39Z str, REQ037 2026-08-17T19:45:30Z str, ISS0109 2026-08-21T03:29:36Z dict. The object appears on the FOURTH use, five days and three string-shaped uses after the first. The rhetorical claim is built on a wrong ordinal. FIX: state the measured figures -- four occurrences, four runs, three key names, two key positions (18/18 and 11/18), two shapes with the object appearing on the fourth and most recent use -- and, if the five-incident frequency is wanted, say it separately as five DEATH incidents across five runs, four of which improvised a key. Filed at BLOCKER per this handoff's own acceptance criterion: the next agent inherits the misquote, and this is the fourth firing of docs/anti-patterns.md's "Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source" -- here inside the very amendment warned about it. The DECISION the numbers support is unaffected; only the numbers are wrong.

CHECK (7). Section 2's schema block was valid, machine-parseable JSON before this commit and is not after it, and DOC-UPDATER's own MINOR justifies the change on the opposite premise. MEASURED: extract the first ```json fence from docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md at each revision and json.loads it -- 131aba9^ -> PARSES, 17 top-level keys; 131aba9 -> "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 48 column 3", i.e. the three // comment lines at lines 125-127. The placeholders cited as proof it was already unparseable (<uuid-v4>, <AGENT_ID>, <ISO8601-UTC or null>) are all INSIDE double-quoted strings and are perfectly legal JSON; that is why the block parsed. So a schema block agents read as a contract lost machine-readability, on a false premise, in the same amendment that argues its own rule is worth having because it is greppable and lintable, and that names mix letflow.lint_handoffs as the enforcement surface. FIX: move the three // lines out of the fence as a prose paragraph immediately beneath it, keeping the field itself in the block. Restores parseability with no loss of visibility at the point of use, and closes the MINOR rather than recording it.

CHECK (2). Section 3's exception column sends THREE fields to section 4.1 -- completed_at, status, result -- but 4.1(a-2)'s normative text authorizes only one: "So ORCH, and only ORCH, writes the `result` block, marked per (b)." ORCH's authority over completed_at and over setting status to COMPLETED appears nowhere as a rule; it survives only as an illustrative value in 4.1(b)'s fields_written row (e.g. ["status","completed_at","result"]) and in section 2's example array. This is the exact drift check (2) predicts: the pointer is stated in one section and its target is incomplete in the other. It matters concretely, twice over. (a) The amendment's own motivating incident is ORCH writing completed_at WITHOUT declaring it (section 3, lines 265-273) -- the field whose undeclared reconstruction prompted the rule is the field the new exception clause never explicitly licenses. (b) A weak model reading 4.1(a-2) literally writes result and leaves status PENDING with completed_at null, reproducing WF02-REQ043-20260818's defect that the paragraph three lines above it rejects by measurement. RELATED, MINOR, same paragraph pair: WF02-REQ043 is cited as the (a-2) reconstruct exemplar at lines 358-365 and as the mid-action (a-1) exemplar at line 425. CHECK (6). The optional-by-absence design is unsound as written, and its failure is already on disk. 4.1(b) states without qualification: "Its absence carries meaning: absence asserts that the result is the acting agent's own report." MEASURED: 546 handoff files predate this rule (547 handoff JSON files at 131aba9, excluding registry.json, of which 1 is this run's own), none audited, so absence in them means "the rule did not exist yet" -- not attestation. That is not a theoretical gap: handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json IS a reconstruction, carries orch_reconstruction rather than not_agent_attested, and 4.1(b) forbids backfilling it. So `grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/` -- the command 4.1(b) offers as the field's entire justification, "enumerates every reconstructed handoff in one command" -- returns ZERO reconstructions in a repository that contains one, permanently. The no-backfill rationale ("a marker retro-fitted to a file nobody can now attest to would itself be an unattested claim") is right in general and wrong for this one file, where the reconstructing agent's own evidence is already in the file. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, both parts needed: (1) date-scope the assertion -- absence carries the attestation claim only for handoffs created on or after the rule's date, and files before it are explicitly unaudited, which costs one sentence and makes the greppability claim honest; (2) name the ISS-0109 file as the single exception to no-backfill -- renaming orch_reconstruction to not_agent_attested and adding fields_written: ["status","completed_at","result"] is a key rename over evidence that is already present and already ORCH's own, not a retro-fitted claim. Without (1) the rule asserts something false about 546 files; without (2) the enumeration command is empty on day one.

CHECK (2), modality drift between section 2 and 4.1. Section 2's comment (line 125) reads "present ONLY on a handoff recovered under section 4.1" and labels the field OPTIONAL, while 4.1(a-1) says a redispatch writes NO marker "because nothing was reconstructed" and 4.1(b) says a handoff completed under (a-2) MUST carry it. FIX: "present ONLY on a handoff reconstructed under section 4.1(a-2); a 4.1(a-1) redispatch does not carry it." Member names themselves do not drift -- all six match 4.1(b)'s table exactly, in the same order.

CHECK (ii)/(6), stale headcount. 4.1(b) says "All 534 handoff files currently in handoffs/ remain valid unchanged." The deeper point is the one to fix: this is a monotonically growing count written into a protocol as a fixed figure, so it is wrong again by the next run.
